Hi Ben and Laura,

Looping you in for the upcoming technical screen with Jordan Park (resume attached). This is the standard backend/ML screen: 60 minutes, dual problem (systems + small model debugging), followed by a 15-minute candidate questions block.

We have tentatively scheduled the interview for 2026-09-15 11:00 AM PT. Jordan confirmed that slot and prefers Zoom or Google Meet + an interactive coding pad.

Attachments: jordan-park-resume.pdf
Also attaching the draft rubric I use for consistency: techscreen-rubric-v2.pdf (please review).

Ben — can you confirm the interviewer lineup? I suggested: Ben (lead), Dev (systems follow-up), Laura (model questions + debrief owner). If any conflicts, let me know. Laura, Ben: please review the rubric and add any model-specific checkpoints you want on the doc in Drive.

Platform: we'll use CoderPad for the coding exercise (link below). Candidate prefers no preloaded libs other than numpy/pandas.
CoderPad session: https://coderpad.io/session/9a2b4c
Meet link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-abcq

Thanks — Mina

Quick notes after skimming the rubric:
- Add an explicit question around model KV cache behavior when scaling sequence length (I can take that).
- For scoring: let's keep 1-4 scale but add a column for "blocker? (Y/N)" so hiring managers can quickly filter urgent fails.

Laura — can you add one model-interpretability checkpoint to the rubric (a short bullet) so we can evaluate reasoning about gradient vs approximation issues?

Also: I'll set up the CoderPad session as a shared interviewer so we can drop in if handoffs are needed. Mina, will you forward the candidate the Meet link and CoderPad invite? I want the candidate to have both.

Ben

Thanks for the ping. I can attend and will own the debrief notes. A few quick asks: 

- Can we provision the CoderPad with a starter repo that includes the simple model code and a tiny dataset? Saves 5-7 minutes during the screen. If not, I'll have the candidate run the small script in the pad.
- I'll add the interpretability checkpoint to the rubric. My proposed bullet: "Explains whether gradient-based attribution would reliably surface token-level importance for the presented failure case; suggests a lightweight sanity check." Keep it short.
- For scoring: agreed on "blocker?" column. I also prefer separate "systems" and "model reasoning" sub-scores so we can see where a candidate strengths/weaknesses lie.

Ben — when you set up the CoderPad, please add Dev as an editor. Dev, if you can drop two quick systems follow-up prompts (disk/network edge case + KV cache rollover), that'll help.

I uploaded a quick prep checklist to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A_sample_briefs (put rubric edits there).

Laura
